optimization_loop.best_description: Evidence-first workflow for engineering and technical research. Verifies version-matched documentation and current file state before writing, works in small steps with short receipts, diagnoses failures from evidence instead of guessing, and reports only checks that actually ran. Use whenever editing code or configuration, calling an API, SDK, CLI or library, debugging or fixing tests, answering technical questions whose answer depends on exact versions or behavior, analyzing data, or writing technical documentation, including small, familiar or urgent changes. Not needed for casual conversation, brainstorming, or non-technical writing.

Use this skill when the user asks you to change, fix, or add to code, config, infrastructure, or docs in a real project, even if the change looks small, routine, or urgent. This includes: editing settings or config values, tuning timeouts or client options, fixing builds, Dockerfiles, or CI workflows, chasing flaky or failing tests, and updating documentation so it matches current code behavior. It also covers questions or calls whose correct answer depends on an exact library, SDK, CLI, or API version, and analysis of data files. The skill checks the real files and versions before acting. Skip it for casual chat, brainstorming, creative or marketing copy, translation, and general reading recommendations.
